NIGERIAN PORTS AUTHORITY

DIRECTORATE OF LEGAL AND REGULATORY SERVICES

REGULATORY DIRECTIVE NO. NPA/DRLS/RD/2026/04

SUBJECT: GENERAL PROVISIONS FOR PORT OPERATIONS, SAFETY, AND COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES WITHIN NIGERIAN PORTS

DATE OF ISSUE: 13 FEBRUARY 2026

DISTRIBUTION: All Terminal Operators, Shipping Lines, Stevedores, Clearing Agents, Port Users, and Relevant Stakeholders.

1.0 LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND AUTHORITY

1.1 The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) derives its regulatory_authority from the Nigerian Ports Authority Act. Record status: current. This Directive is issued pursuant to the powers conferred upon the Authority under the said Act, and any subsidiary legislation made thereunder, for the purpose of ensuring the efficient, safe, and orderly management of all ports within the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

1.2 This Directive shall apply to all persons, vessels, vehicles, goods, and equipment within the jurisdiction of the Authority, including all port premises, approaches, and navigable channels under the control of the NPA.

1.3 Nothing in this Directive shall be construed as derogating from the provisions of any other applicable law, including but not limited to the Merchant Shipping Act, the Customs and Excise Management Act, and international conventions to which Nigeria is a party.

2.0 DEFINITIONS

In this Directive, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Authority" means the Nigerian Ports Authority.

"Port Premises" means all land, water, buildings, structures, and facilities owned, leased, or operated by the Authority or licensed operators within port limits.

"Operator" means any person or entity licensed by the Authority to provide port services, including terminal operations, stevedoring, pilotage, towage, and shore handling.

"User" means any person, shipping line, agent, or consignee utilizing port facilities or services.

"Vessel" includes any ship, craft, lighter, barge, or floating structure.

3.0 GENERAL OBLIGATIONS OF OPERATORS AND USERS

3.1 Every Operator shall maintain valid licenses, permits, and approvals issued by the Authority for the conduct of their activities. Licenses shall be prominently displayed at the place of business and made available for inspection upon request by an authorized officer of the Authority.

3.2 Operators shall comply with all safety, security, and environmental standards prescribed by the Authority and by other relevant agencies of the Federal Government.

3.3 Users shall ensure that all documentation relating to vessels, cargo, and personnel is complete, accurate, and submitted within the timelines specified in relevant NPA guidelines.

3.4 No person shall obstruct, impede, or interfere with the lawful operations of the Authority or any licensed Operator within port premises.

4.0 VESSEL MOVEMENTS AND NAVIGATION

4.1 All vessels entering, leaving, or moving within port limits shall comply with the directions of the Harbour Master and shall utilize the services of authorized pilots where pilotage is compulsory.

4.2 Vessels shall maintain radio contact with the Port Control Station on the designated VHF channels at all times while within port limits.

4.3 The master of any vessel shall give notice of arrival, expected time of berthing, and estimated time of departure in accordance with the procedures set out in the NPA Port Marine Operations Manual.

4.4 Anchoring is permitted only in designated anchorages. No vessel shall anchor or moor in navigable channels or in any area not designated for that purpose without prior approval.
2.3 Amendment of Clause 4.3 – Notice of Arrival

Clause 4.3 of the General Provisions is hereby amended by the substitution of the words "in accordance with the procedures set out in the NPA Port Marine Operations Manual" with the words "in accordance with the procedures set out in the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01), which shall be the operative reference for all vessel movement procedures."

2.4 Insertion of New Clause 4.5 – Vessel Traffic Services

A new Clause 4.5 is hereby inserted after Clause 4.4, as follows:

"4.5 All vessels within port limits shall participate in the Vessel Traffic Services (VTS) system operated by the Authority. Vessels shall comply with all instructions issued by the VTS operator, including instructions relating to speed, course, and position reporting. Failure to comply with VTS instructions shall constitute a breach of these General Provisions."

3.0 GENERAL OBLIGATIONS – ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

3.1 Every Operator shall, within thirty (30) days of the effective date of this Directive, submit to the Authority a compliance statement confirming that their operations conform to the provisions of the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

3.2 Operators shall designate a named individual as their Compliance Officer who shall be responsible for ensuring adherence to the provisions of the Manual and this Directive. The name and contact details of the Compliance Officer shall be provided to the Authority in writing.

3.3 Users shall ensure that all cargo documentation, including manifests, bills of lading, and customs declarations, are submitted electronically through the port community system in accordance with the timelines specified in the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

Port Operations Manual 2025 revision_date 2025-11-01 date. Record status: historical.

4.0 ENFORCEMENT AND PENALTIES

4.1 Any Operator or User who contravenes any provision of this Directive or of the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01) shall be liable to such penalties as may be prescribed by the Authority, including but not limited to fines, suspension of licenses, or revocation of licenses.

4.2 The Authority may, by notice in writing, require an Operator to remedy any deficiency in its operations within a specified period. Failure to remedy such deficiency within the specified period shall constitute a breach of these General Provisions.

4.3 Nothing in this Directive shall be construed as limiting the powers of the Authority to take such other enforcement action as may be provided for under the Nigerian Ports Authority Act or any other law.

5.0 TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

5.1 For the avoidance of doubt, any reference in any existing regulation, directive, or guideline issued by the Authority to the "NPA Port Marine Operations Manual" or any previous version of port operations procedures shall be construed as a reference to the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

5.2 All licenses, permits, and approvals issued prior to the effective date of this Directive shall remain valid subject to compliance with the provisions of this Directive and the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

5.3 Any pending applications for licenses, permits, or approvals shall be processed in accordance with the provisions of this Directive and the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01) upon the effective date.
NIGERIAN PORTS AUTHORITY

REGULATORY DIRECTIVE – GENERAL PROVISIONS

DIRECTIVE NO: NPA/RD/GEN/2026/03
ISSUE DATE: 2026-03-18
EFFECTIVE DATE: 2026-04-01

6.0 ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS

6.1 Appointment and Designation of the Harbour Master

6.1.1 Pursuant to section 7(2)(c) of the Nigerian Ports Authority Act and in exercise of the powers conferred on the Authority under the said Act, the Authority hereby confirms the appointment of Captain Adebayo Ogunlesi as Harbour Master. Captain Adebayo Ogunlesi holds the role_title of Harbour Master, per the NPA directive. Record status: current. This appointment is current and shall remain in force until revoked or superseded by a subsequent directive of the Authority.

6.1.2 The Harbour Master shall exercise all powers and perform all duties conferred or imposed upon the Harbour Master by the Act, these General Provisions, the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01), and any other subsidiary legislation issued by the Authority.

6.1.3 The Harbour Master shall, in particular, be responsible for:
(a) the safe and efficient movement of vessels within port limits, including berthing, unberthing, and anchorage assignments;
(b) the enforcement of port marine regulations, including compliance with the Collision Regulations (COLREGs) as adopted by Nigeria;
(c) the coordination of search and rescue operations within port limits;
(d) the issuance of berthing permits and the approval of special operations, including bunkering, ship-to-ship transfers, and over-dimensional cargo movements;
(e) the maintenance of the port's navigational aids and the reporting of any defects or obstructions to the Chief Engineer;
(f) the investigation of marine incidents, near-misses, and pollution events, and the submission of investigation reports to the Authority within the timelines prescribed in the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

6.1.4 All Operators and Users shall cooperate with the Harbour Master in the discharge of his duties. Any instruction given by the Harbour Master in the exercise of his statutory functions shall be complied with promptly, subject to any right of appeal to the Authority in writing.

6.2 Authorised Officers

6.2.1 The Authority may designate, by notice in the port community system, such other officers as it deems fit to exercise specific powers under this Directive, including powers of inspection, verification of documentation, and enforcement of health, safety, and environmental requirements.

6.2.2 A notice issued under paragraph 6.2.1 shall specify the name and designation of the officer, the powers delegated, and the duration of the delegation.

7.0 COMMUNICATION AND NOTICES

7.1 Method of Service

7.1.1 Any notice, directive, or communication required to be given under this Directive shall be in writing and shall be served:
(a) by personal delivery to the registered office or principal place of business of the Operator or User;
(b) by registered post or courier to the last known address of the Operator or User;
(c) by electronic mail to the address provided by the Operator or User in the port community system; or
(d) by publication on the Authority's official website, where the Authority considers that the notice is of general application.

7.1.2 A notice served by electronic mail shall be deemed to have been received on the next working day following transmission, unless the Authority receives a delivery failure notification.
8.0 ENFORCEMENT

8.1 Powers of the Authority

8.1.1 Without prejudice to the powers conferred on the Authority by the Nigerian Ports Authority Act, Cap. N126, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, and any other enactment, the Authority may take such enforcement action as it considers necessary to secure compliance with this Directive and with any notice, permit, licence, or approval issued under it.

8.1.2 Enforcement action may include, but shall not be limited to:
(a) the issue of a written warning specifying the nature of the non-compliance and the period within which it must be remedied;
(b) the suspension, revocation, or non-renewal of any permit, licence, berth allocation, or service approval granted by the Authority;
(c) the refusal of port entry, berthing, or cargo clearance;
(d) the imposition of administrative fines or penalties in accordance with the schedule prescribed by the Authority and published in the port community system;
(e) the detention of a vessel or the impounding of cargo, equipment, or documents, pending the resolution of the non-compliance; and
(f) the initiation of legal proceedings.

8.1.3 The Authority shall, before taking any enforcement action under paragraph 8.1.2(b), (d), or (e), give the Operator or User concerned a written notice of its intention, stating the grounds for the proposed action and affording the Operator or User a reasonable opportunity, not being less than seven working days, to make representations. This paragraph shall not apply where the Authority reasonably considers that there is an imminent risk to safety, security, or the environment.

8.2 Non-Compliance by Vessels

8.2.1 Where a vessel is found to be in breach of any provision of this Directive, or of any applicable international convention to which Nigeria is a party, the Authority may, in addition to any other action, direct the Master, Owner, or Agent to take corrective measures within a specified period.

8.2.2 Failure to comply with a direction issued under paragraph 8.2.1 may result in the vessel being prohibited from sailing until the corrective measures are completed to the satisfaction of the Authority.

8.3 Obstruction of Authorised Officers

8.3.1 No person shall willfully obstruct, hinder, or delay any Authorised Officer in the performance of his duties under this Directive, or fail to produce any document, record, or information lawfully required by such officer.

8.3.2 Any person who contravenes paragraph 8.3.1 shall be liable to such penalties as may be prescribed by the Authority, without prejudice to any other liability under law.

9.0 COMPLIANCE AND AUDIT

9.1 Duty to Comply

9.1.1 Every Operator and User shall comply with the provisions of this Directive, the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01), and any other applicable regulations, guidelines, or standards issued by the Authority from time to time.

9.1.2 Compliance with this Directive does not relieve any Operator or User of the obligation to comply with any other applicable law, regulation, or international convention.

9.2 Record-Keeping

9.2.1 Every Operator and User shall maintain accurate and up-to-date records relating to its operations within the port, including but not limited to:
(a) vessel arrival and departure times, berthing schedules, and cargo manifests;
(b) crew lists and passenger lists;
(c) records of hazardous cargo, including safety data sheets and stowage plans;
(d) maintenance and inspection records for equipment and facilities;
(e) records of waste disposal and pollution prevention measures; and
(f) incident reports and investigation records.
9.3 Audits and Inspections

9.3.1 The Authority may, at any reasonable time, conduct audits and inspections of any Operator or User to verify compliance with this Directive and any other applicable regulations.

9.3.2 Audits and inspections may be announced or unannounced. Where an audit or inspection is announced, the Authority shall give the Operator or User not less than seven (7) days' written notice, unless the Authority determines that a shorter notice period is necessary to address a risk to safety, security, or the environment.

9.3.3 An Operator or User shall provide all reasonable assistance to an Authorised Officer conducting an audit or inspection, including access to premises, facilities, equipment, records, and personnel.

9.3.4 Where an audit or inspection reveals a deficiency or non-compliance, the Authority may issue a corrective action plan requiring the Operator or User to address the deficiency within a specified period.

9.4 Reporting Obligations

9.4.1 Every Operator and User shall report to the Authority, in the manner and form prescribed, any incident, accident, or near-miss occurring within the port that involves or may involve any of the following:
(a) death or serious injury to any person;
(b) significant damage to property, equipment, or infrastructure;
(c) pollution or a threat of pollution to the marine environment;
(d) a breach of security; or
(e) any other matter that the Authority may prescribe.

9.4.2 A report under paragraph 9.4.1 shall be made as soon as practicable and, in any event, not later than twenty-four (24) hours after the occurrence, unless a longer period is authorised by the Authority.

9.4.3 Nothing in this paragraph shall prevent or delay any immediate action that may be necessary to protect life, property, or the environment.

10.0 AMENDMENTS AND UPDATES

10.1 General Provisions for Amendments

10.1.1 The Authority may, from time to time, amend, vary, or update this Directive, in whole or in part, as it considers necessary or expedient for the efficient and safe operation of the port, or for the purpose of giving effect to any international convention, national law, or policy.

10.1.2 Amendments to this Directive shall be issued in writing by the Authority and shall take effect on the date specified in the amendment notice, or, where no date is specified, on the date of publication.

10.1.3 Without prejudice to paragraph 10.1.2, the Authority may, where it considers it necessary for the protection of safety, security, or the environment, give effect to an amendment with immediate effect and shall, in such a case, notify all affected Operators and Users as soon as practicable.

10.1.4 An amendment to this Directive shall not operate retrospectively to the detriment of any person, unless the amendment is made to give effect to a provision of an international convention or national law that expressly requires retrospective application.

10.1.5 Where an amendment affects the rights or obligations of any Operator or User, the Authority shall, to the extent practicable, give not less than thirty (30) days' notice of the amendment before it takes effect.

10.2 Notification of Amendments

10.2.1 The Authority shall publish amendments to this Directive on its official website and may also notify affected Operators and Users by circular, electronic mail, or other means of communication.

10.2.2 It shall be the responsibility of every Operator and User to keep itself informed of any amendments to this Directive and to comply with the Directive as amended.

1.0 PURPOSE
This report provides a consolidated overview of the fixed infrastructure assets under the purview of the LPC Engineering Department as at the end of June 2026. It serves as the baseline reference for the detailed weekly maintenance schedules, inspection findings, and repair logs issued separately during the period. The information herein reflects the current registered status of all assets and is to be used for planning, budgeting, and operational coordination with the Port Operations and Marine Services departments.

2.0 PORT INFRASTRUCTURE SUMMARY

2.1 Berths
Apapa Port has a berth_count of 12 berths, according to the engineering maintenance report. Record status: current. This count is the current registered configuration and has been in effect since the completion of the Berth 11 and 12 extension project in Q1 2025. No change to the number of operational berths is scheduled for the current financial year. The berths are designated as follows:

All berth designations, fender types, bollard capacities, and crane rail alignments are recorded in the Asset Register (Reference: LPC/ENGR/AR/2026-06). Any deviation from the registered configuration must be reported to the Deputy Chief Engineer (Infrastructure) within 24 hours.

2.2 Quay Walls and Apron
The total quay length is 2,850 linear metres. The quay wall structure is a combination of anchored sheet pile (Berths 01–07) and concrete caisson (Berths 08–12). The apron width varies between 25 and 40 metres. A routine visual inspection of the quay walls was carried out in the week of 15 June 2026. No structural defects requiring immediate intervention were noted. Minor spalling was observed at the expansion joint between Berth 05 and Berth 06; this has been logged for scheduled repair under Work Order WO-2026-0841.

2.3 Fendering Systems
The port utilises a mix of cone and cell fenders across all 12 berths. The fender inventory, including spare units, is maintained at the Engineering Stores. The following table summarises the fender types and their installation dates:

2.4 Bollards
A total of 96 bollards are installed across the 12 berths, with a nominal capacity of 100 tonnes each for the container and general cargo berths, and 150 tonnes for the bulk liquid berths. A load test verification of all bollards was last completed in November 2025. The test certificates are archived in the Engineering Document Control system. Bollard condition is checked during the weekly quay walkdown; the findings for June 2026 are recorded in the weekly inspection logs referenced in Section 5.0.

3.0 CRANE RAILS AND PAVEMENT

3.1 Crane Rails
The crane rail tracks for the ship-to-shore (STS) gantry cranes are laid on concrete beams. The rail alignment and gauge were surveyed in May 2026. The survey confirmed that the rail gauge is within the tolerance of ±5 mm across all berths. Rail wear measurements were taken at designated points; the maximum recorded wear is 8 mm on the landside rail at Berth 07. This is within the allowable wear limit of 12 mm. The next full rail survey is scheduled for November 2026.

3.2 Pavement
The container yard pavement (concrete interlocking blocks) is generally in good condition. Areas of settlement were previously identified at Yard B (near the reefer points). A patch repair was completed in March 2026. A follow-up inspection on 20 June 2026 confirmed that the repaired area is stable. No new significant settlement was observed in June. The asphalt pavement at the RoRo berth approach is scheduled for resurfacing in Q4 2026; the scope of work is being prepared by the Civil Engineering Unit.
**4.1 Berth Condition Summary**

The quay walls and berth structures were inspected during the monthly marine structures walkdown conducted on 22–23 June 2026. The inspection covered all 12 berths, with particular attention to the concrete copings, expansion joints, and the anchorages of the mooring hardware. The general condition of the concrete structures remains satisfactory, with no new structural defects identified beyond those previously logged. **4.2 Berth 5 Apapa – Maintenance Status**

Berth 5 Apapa maintenance_status scheduled maintenance. Record status: current. The scheduled maintenance for Berth 5 Apapa is currently active and has been planned to address the following scope of works:

- Replacement of the two neoprene bearing pads at the berth's western end, which have shown signs of compression set beyond the acceptable limit.
- Re-grouting of the anchor bolts for the bollards at positions B5-04 and B5-05.
- Application of a protective coating to the concrete coping along a 40-metre section where the existing coating has deteriorated.

The maintenance window is scheduled for 10–24 August 2026. During this period, Berth 5 Apapa will be unavailable for vessel berthing. The berthing schedule for this period has been adjusted by the Port Operations department to redistribute calls to Berths 4 and 6. The Engineering Department will issue a Notice to Mariners (NTM) and a port circular at least 14 days prior to the commencement of the works. The berth will be handed back to operations following a joint inspection by the Engineering Department and the Port Captain's office, which is planned for 25 August 2026.

**4.3 Mooring Hardware and Ancillary Equipment**

The inspection of mooring hardware, including bitts, quick-release hooks, and capstans, was completed on 24 June 2026. The findings are recorded below:

- **Quick-release hooks (QRH):** All 24 QRH units across the berths were functionally tested. Two units at Berth 09 were found to have a slower-than-specified release time and have been flagged for servicing. The servicing is scheduled for the next available maintenance window in July 2026.
- **Capstans:** The capstan motors at Berths 02, 07, and 11 were checked for current draw and temperature. All readings were within the normal operating range.
- **Bitts and bollards:** Visual inspection of the bitts and bollards found no signs of deformation or cracking. The bollard load test certificates remain valid as per the November 2025 verification.
The servicing has been rescheduled for the week commencing 19 October 2026, subject to parts receipt. Until the servicing is completed, the two QRH units at Berth 09 will remain in service but are subject to an operational restriction: they must be manually cycled once per shift to ensure the release mechanism does not seize. The Port Operations department has been notified of this restriction via internal memo dated 24 September 2026. The units will be re-tested for release time following the servicing.

2.3 Routine Inspections – September 2026

Routine visual inspections of all berth structures were carried out on 15 September 2026. No new structural defects were identified. The condition of fenders, mooring hooks, and bollard foundations remains consistent with the previous reporting period. The bollard load test certificates remain valid as per the November 2025 verification.

3.1 Quay Crane 7 – Status and Inspection Record

Quay Crane 7 has a load_capacity_tons of 50 metric tons, according to the maintenance report. Record status: current. This rating is current and forms the basis for all operational load planning and lifting procedure approvals. No change to this rating is planned.

The crane was subject to its periodic three-monthly inspection on 10 September 2026. The inspection focused on the hoist braking system, the main trolley travel mechanism, and the condition of the wire ropes. The findings are as follows:

- **Hoist brakes:** The brake pads were measured at 70% of their original thickness, which is within the acceptable wear limit. The brake adjustment was verified and found to be within specification.
- **Trolley travel:** The travel wheels showed no abnormal wear. The rail alignment was checked and found to be within the tolerance of ±2 mm over the full length of travel.
- **Wire ropes:** The main hoist wire rope was inspected for broken wires and diameter reduction. No defects were found. The rope lubrication was topped up as part of the inspection.

A minor oil leak was observed on the slew gearbox oil seal. The leak is currently minor and does not affect the safe operation of the crane. The seal (Part No. SG-SE-118) has been ordered, and the replacement is scheduled for the next maintenance window in November 2026. The gearbox oil level is being monitored weekly until the seal is replaced.

The crane has been fully operational throughout the reporting period. No unplanned downtime was recorded.

4.0 PAVEMENT AND ROAD NETWORK

4.1 Container Yard Paving Repairs

The repair of the pavement in the container yard, specifically the area adjacent to the reefer stacks, was completed on 18 September 2026. The works involved the removal and replacement of a 25-square-metre section of concrete paving that had settled. The new concrete has been cured and is now open to traffic. The repaired area has been marked with temporary paint and will be monitored for any signs of settlement over the next three months.

**5.0 DRAINAGE AND UTILITIES**

**5.1 Storm Water Drainage System**

Routine inspection of the main storm water drainage network was carried out on 14 August 2026. The inspection covered all open channels, culverts, and catch basins within the terminal operating area.

Findings:

- **Main outfall channel:** Clear of obstruction. Flow capacity assessed as adequate for current rainfall intensity.
- **Catch basins (Berths 1–4):** Two basins (CB-02 and CB-04) were found to be 40% silted. Desilting was carried out on 19 August 2026. Both basins are now clear.
- **Culvert under access road (Gate 2):** Minor cracking observed in the concrete headwall. Crack width measured at 2 mm. No active water ingress noted. The headwall is scheduled for patching during the November maintenance window.

No storm water pumping stations are currently out of service.

**5.2 Potable Water Supply**

The main potable water storage tank (Tank WT-01) was cleaned and disinfected on 27 July 2026. Water quality samples taken after cleaning were within WHO guidelines. The tank level control valve was serviced on the same date.

A leak was reported on the supply line serving the administration building on 3 September 2026. The leak was traced to a failed joint at the boundary wall. The joint was replaced on 5 September 2026. No further leaks have been reported.

**5.3 Sewerage System**

The sewage pumping station (SPS-01) serving the terminal buildings was inspected on 22 September 2026. Both pumps were found operational. Pump No. 2 was noted to have a higher than normal vibration level. Vibration analysis is scheduled for the next maintenance window. The station is operating normally.

**6.0 FENCING AND ACCESS CONTROL**

**6.1 Perimeter Fencing**

The perimeter fence along the eastern boundary was inspected on 11 August 2026. The inspection covered the full 1,200-metre length.

- **Concrete posts:** All posts in good condition.
- **Chain link mesh:** Two small breaches were found near the old customs checkpoint. These were repaired on 12 August 2026.
- **Barbed wire topping:** Intact throughout.

**6.2 Access Gates**

The four main access gates (Gates 1–4) were checked for mechanical operation on 17 September 2026. All gates open and close smoothly. Gate 3 hydraulic ram was found to be leaking a small amount of hydraulic fluid. The ram has been ordered (Part No. HR-G3-220) and will be replaced during the November maintenance window. The leak is minor and does not affect safe operation of the gate.

**7.0 BUILDING INFRASTRUCTURE**

**7.1 Administration Building**

Routine inspection of the administration building was carried out on 8 September 2026.

- **Roof:** No leaks reported. The roof drainage gutters were cleared of debris.
- **Air conditioning units:** All units serviced on 15 July 2026. Filters replaced. Units operating normally.
- **Electrical distribution board:** Thermal imaging scan carried out on 8 September 2026. No hot spots detected.

**7.2 Workshop Building**

The main workshop building roof was inspected on 21 August 2026 following a period of heavy rain. No leaks were found. The roller shutter doors were checked for operation. Door No. 2 was found to have a worn track. The track was replaced on 25 August 2026.

NIGERIAN PORTS AUTHORITY

DIRECTORATE OF LEGAL AND REGULATORY SERVICES

REGULATORY DIRECTIVE NO. NPA/DRLS/RD/2026/04

SUBJECT: GENERAL PROVISIONS FOR PORT OPERATIONS, SAFETY, AND COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES WITHIN NIGERIAN PORTS

DATE OF ISSUE: 13 FEBRUARY 2026

DISTRIBUTION: All Terminal Operators, Shipping Lines, Stevedores, Clearing Agents, Port Users, and Relevant Stakeholders.

1.0 LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND AUTHORITY

1.1 The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) derives its regulatory_authority from the Nigerian Ports Authority Act. Record status: current. This Directive is issued pursuant to the powers conferred upon the Authority under the said Act, and any subsidiary legislation made thereunder, for the purpose of ensuring the efficient, safe, and orderly management of all ports within the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

1.2 This Directive shall apply to all persons, vessels, vehicles, goods, and equipment within the jurisdiction of the Authority, including all port premises, approaches, and navigable channels under the control of the NPA.

1.3 Nothing in this Directive shall be construed as derogating from the provisions of any other applicable law, including but not limited to the Merchant Shipping Act, the Customs and Excise Management Act, and international conventions to which Nigeria is a party.

2.0 DEFINITIONS

In this Directive, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Authority" means the Nigerian Ports Authority.

"Port Premises" means all land, water, buildings, structures, and facilities owned, leased, or operated by the Authority or licensed operators within port limits.

"Operator" means any person or entity licensed by the Authority to provide port services, including terminal operations, stevedoring, pilotage, towage, and shore handling.

"User" means any person, shipping line, agent, or consignee utilizing port facilities or services.

"Vessel" includes any ship, craft, lighter, barge, or floating structure.

3.0 GENERAL OBLIGATIONS OF OPERATORS AND USERS

3.1 Every Operator shall maintain valid licenses, permits, and approvals issued by the Authority for the conduct of their activities. Licenses shall be prominently displayed at the place of business and made available for inspection upon request by an authorized officer of the Authority.

3.2 Operators shall comply with all safety, security, and environmental standards prescribed by the Authority and by other relevant agencies of the Federal Government.

3.3 Users shall ensure that all documentation relating to vessels, cargo, and personnel is complete, accurate, and submitted within the timelines specified in relevant NPA guidelines.

3.4 No person shall obstruct, impede, or interfere with the lawful operations of the Authority or any licensed Operator within port premises.

4.0 VESSEL MOVEMENTS AND NAVIGATION

4.1 All vessels entering, leaving, or moving within port limits shall comply with the directions of the Harbour Master and shall utilize the services of authorized pilots where pilotage is compulsory.

4.2 Vessels shall maintain radio contact with the Port Control Station on the designated VHF channels at all times while within port limits.

4.3 The master of any vessel shall give notice of arrival, expected time of berthing, and estimated time of departure in accordance with the procedures set out in the NPA Port Marine Operations Manual.

4.4 Anchoring is permitted only in designated anchorages. No vessel shall anchor or moor in navigable channels or in any area not designated for that purpose without prior approval.

2.4 Insertion of New Clause 4.5 – Vessel Traffic Services

A new Clause 4.5 is hereby inserted after Clause 4.4, as follows:

"4.5 All vessels within port limits shall participate in the Vessel Traffic Services (VTS) system operated by the Authority. Vessels shall comply with all instructions issued by the VTS operator, including instructions relating to speed, course, and position reporting. Failure to comply with VTS instructions shall constitute a breach of these General Provisions."

3.0 GENERAL OBLIGATIONS – ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

3.1 Every Operator shall, within thirty (30) days of the effective date of this Directive, submit to the Authority a compliance statement confirming that their operations conform to the provisions of the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

3.2 Operators shall designate a named individual as their Compliance Officer who shall be responsible for ensuring adherence to the provisions of the Manual and this Directive. The name and contact details of the Compliance Officer shall be provided to the Authority in writing.

3.3 Users shall ensure that all cargo documentation, including manifests, bills of lading, and customs declarations, are submitted electronically through the port community system in accordance with the timelines specified in the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

4.0 ENFORCEMENT AND PENALTIES

4.1 Any Operator or User who contravenes any provision of this Directive or of the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01) shall be liable to such penalties as may be prescribed by the Authority, including but not limited to fines, suspension of licenses, or revocation of licenses.

4.2 The Authority may, by notice in writing, require an Operator to remedy any deficiency in its operations within a specified period. Failure to remedy such deficiency within the specified period shall constitute a breach of these General Provisions.

4.3 Nothing in this Directive shall be construed as limiting the powers of the Authority to take such other enforcement action as may be provided for under the Nigerian Ports Authority Act or any other law.

5.0 TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

5.1 For the avoidance of doubt, any reference in any existing regulation, directive, or guideline issued by the Authority to the "NPA Port Marine Operations Manual" or any previous version of port operations procedures shall be construed as a reference to the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

5.2 All licenses, permits, and approvals issued prior to the effective date of this Directive shall remain valid subject to compliance with the provisions of this Directive and the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

5.3 Any pending applications for licenses, permits, or approvals shall be processed in accordance with the provisions of this Directive and the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01) upon the effective date.

6.0 ADMINISTRATIVE PROVISIONS

6.1 Appointment and Designation of the Harbour Master

6.1.1 Pursuant to section 7(2)(c) of the Nigerian Ports Authority Act and in exercise of the powers conferred on the Authority under the said Act, the Authority hereby confirms the appointment of Captain Adebayo Ogunlesi as Harbour Master. Captain Adebayo Ogunlesi holds the role_title of Harbour Master, per the NPA directive. Record status: current. This appointment is current and shall remain in force until revoked or superseded by a subsequent directive of the Authority.

6.1.2 The Harbour Master shall exercise all powers and perform all duties conferred or imposed upon the Harbour Master by the Act, these General Provisions, the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01), and any other subsidiary legislation issued by the Authority.

6.1.3 The Harbour Master shall, in particular, be responsible for:
(a) the safe and efficient movement of vessels within port limits, including berthing, unberthing, and anchorage assignments;
(b) the enforcement of port marine regulations, including compliance with the Collision Regulations (COLREGs) as adopted by Nigeria;
(c) the coordination of search and rescue operations within port limits;
(d) the issuance of berthing permits and the approval of special operations, including bunkering, ship-to-ship transfers, and over-dimensional cargo movements;
(e) the maintenance of the port's navigational aids and the reporting of any defects or obstructions to the Chief Engineer;
(f) the investigation of marine incidents, near-misses, and pollution events, and the submission of investigation reports to the Authority within the timelines prescribed in the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01).

6.1.4 All Operators and Users shall cooperate with the Harbour Master in the discharge of his duties. Any instruction given by the Harbour Master in the exercise of his statutory functions shall be complied with promptly, subject to any right of appeal to the Authority in writing.

6.2 Authorised Officers

6.2.1 The Authority may designate, by notice in the port community system, such other officers as it deems fit to exercise specific powers under this Directive, including powers of inspection, verification of documentation, and enforcement of health, safety, and environmental requirements.

6.2.2 A notice issued under paragraph 6.2.1 shall specify the name and designation of the officer, the powers delegated, and the duration of the delegation.

7.0 COMMUNICATION AND NOTICES

7.1 Method of Service

7.1.1 Any notice, directive, or communication required to be given under this Directive shall be in writing and shall be served:
(a) by personal delivery to the registered office or principal place of business of the Operator or User;
(b) by registered post or courier to the last known address of the Operator or User;
(c) by electronic mail to the address provided by the Operator or User in the port community system; or
(d) by publication on the Authority's official website, where the Authority considers that the notice is of general application.

7.1.2 A notice served by electronic mail shall be deemed to have been received on the next working day following transmission, unless the Authority receives a delivery failure notification.

8.0 ENFORCEMENT

8.1 Powers of the Authority

8.1.1 Without prejudice to the powers conferred on the Authority by the Nigerian Ports Authority Act, Cap. N126, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, and any other enactment, the Authority may take such enforcement action as it considers necessary to secure compliance with this Directive and with any notice, permit, licence, or approval issued under it.

8.1.2 Enforcement action may include, but shall not be limited to:
(a) the issue of a written warning specifying the nature of the non-compliance and the period within which it must be remedied;
(b) the suspension, revocation, or non-renewal of any permit, licence, berth allocation, or service approval granted by the Authority;
(c) the refusal of port entry, berthing, or cargo clearance;
(d) the imposition of administrative fines or penalties in accordance with the schedule prescribed by the Authority and published in the port community system;
(e) the detention of a vessel or the impounding of cargo, equipment, or documents, pending the resolution of the non-compliance; and
(f) the initiation of legal proceedings.

8.1.3 The Authority shall, before taking any enforcement action under paragraph 8.1.2(b), (d), or (e), give the Operator or User concerned a written notice of its intention, stating the grounds for the proposed action and affording the Operator or User a reasonable opportunity, not being less than seven working days, to make representations. This paragraph shall not apply where the Authority reasonably considers that there is an imminent risk to safety, security, or the environment.

8.2 Non-Compliance by Vessels

8.2.1 Where a vessel is found to be in breach of any provision of this Directive, or of any applicable international convention to which Nigeria is a party, the Authority may, in addition to any other action, direct the Master, Owner, or Agent to take corrective measures within a specified period.

8.2.2 Failure to comply with a direction issued under paragraph 8.2.1 may result in the vessel being prohibited from sailing until the corrective measures are completed to the satisfaction of the Authority.

8.3 Obstruction of Authorised Officers

8.3.1 No person shall willfully obstruct, hinder, or delay any Authorised Officer in the performance of his duties under this Directive, or fail to produce any document, record, or information lawfully required by such officer.

8.3.2 Any person who contravenes paragraph 8.3.1 shall be liable to such penalties as may be prescribed by the Authority, without prejudice to any other liability under law.

9.0 COMPLIANCE AND AUDIT

9.1 Duty to Comply

9.1.1 Every Operator and User shall comply with the provisions of this Directive, the Port Operations Manual 2025 (revision date 2025-11-01), and any other applicable regulations, guidelines, or standards issued by the Authority from time to time.

9.1.2 Compliance with this Directive does not relieve any Operator or User of the obligation to comply with any other applicable law, regulation, or international convention.

9.2 Record-Keeping

9.2.1 Every Operator and User shall maintain accurate and up-to-date records relating to its operations within the port, including but not limited to:
(a) vessel arrival and departure times, berthing schedules, and cargo manifests;
(b) crew lists and passenger lists;
(c) records of hazardous cargo, including safety data sheets and stowage plans;
(d) maintenance and inspection records for equipment and facilities;
(e) records of waste disposal and pollution prevention measures; and
(f) incident reports and investigation records.

documents.content:
9.3 Audits and Inspections

9.3.1 The Authority may, at any reasonable time, conduct audits and inspections of any Operator or User to verify compliance with this Directive and any other applicable regulations.

9.3.2 Audits and inspections may be announced or unannounced. Where an audit or inspection is announced, the Authority shall give the Operator or User not less than seven (7) days' written notice, unless the Authority determines that a shorter notice period is necessary to address a risk to safety, security, or the environment.

9.3.3 An Operator or User shall provide all reasonable assistance to an Authorised Officer conducting an audit or inspection, including access to premises, facilities, equipment, records, and personnel.

9.3.4 Where an audit or inspection reveals a deficiency or non-compliance, the Authority may issue a corrective action plan requiring the Operator or User to address the deficiency within a specified period.

9.4 Reporting Obligations

9.4.1 Every Operator and User shall report to the Authority, in the manner and form prescribed, any incident, accident, or near-miss occurring within the port that involves or may involve any of the following:
(a) death or serious injury to any person;
(b) significant damage to property, equipment, or infrastructure;
(c) pollution or a threat of pollution to the marine environment;
(d) a breach of security; or
(e) any other matter that the Authority may prescribe.

9.4.2 A report under paragraph 9.4.1 shall be made as soon as practicable and, in any event, not later than twenty-four (24) hours after the occurrence, unless a longer period is authorised by the Authority.

9.4.3 Nothing in this paragraph shall prevent or delay any immediate action that may be necessary to protect life, property, or the environment.

10.0 AMENDMENTS AND UPDATES

10.1 General Provisions for Amendments

10.1.1 The Authority may, from time to time, amend, vary, or update this Directive, in whole or in part, as it considers necessary or expedient for the efficient and safe operation of the port, or for the purpose of giving effect to any international convention, national law, or policy.

10.1.2 Amendments to this Directive shall be issued in writing by the Authority and shall take effect on the date specified in the amendment notice, or, where no date is specified, on the date of publication.

10.1.3 Without prejudice to paragraph 10.1.2, the Authority may, where it considers it necessary for the protection of safety, security, or the environment, give effect to an amendment with immediate effect and shall, in such a case, notify all affected Operators and Users as soon as practicable.

10.1.4 An amendment to this Directive shall not operate retrospectively to the detriment of any person, unless the amendment is made to give effect to a provision of an international convention or national law that expressly requires retrospective application.

10.1.5 Where an amendment affects the rights or obligations of any Operator or User, the Authority shall, to the extent practicable, give not less than thirty (30) days' notice of the amendment before it takes effect.

10.2 Notification of Amendments

10.2.1 The Authority shall publish amendments to this Directive on its official website and may also notify affected Operators and Users by circular, electronic mail, or other means of communication.

10.2.2 It shall be the responsibility of every Operator and User to keep itself informed of any amendments to this Directive and to comply with the Directive as amended.

LPC ENGINEERING DEPARTMENT
MAINTENANCE REPORT – INFRASTRUCTURE OVERVIEW
REPORT NO: LPC/ENGR/INFRA/2026/06-01
PERIOD COVERED: 01 June 2026 – 30 June 2026
ISSUE DATE: 02 July 2026
PREPARED BY: Engr. T. Okafor, Deputy Chief Engineer (Infrastructure)
APPROVED BY: Engr. Mrs. A. Bello, Chief Engineer

1.0 PURPOSE
This report provides a consolidated overview of the fixed infrastructure assets under the purview of the LPC Engineering Department as at the end of June 2026. It serves as the baseline reference for the detailed weekly maintenance schedules, inspection findings, and repair logs issued separately during the period. The information herein reflects the current registered status of all assets and is to be used for planning, budgeting, and operational coordination with the Port Operations and Marine Services departments.

2.0 PORT INFRASTRUCTURE SUMMARY

2.1 Berths
Apapa Port has a berth_count of 12 berths, according to the engineering maintenance report. Record status: current. This count is the current registered configuration and has been in effect since the completion of the Berth 11 and 12 extension project in Q1 2025. No change to the number of operational berths is scheduled for the current financial year. The berths are designated as follows:

All berth designations, fender types, bollard capacities, and crane rail alignments are recorded in the Asset Register (Reference: LPC/ENGR/AR/2026-06). Any deviation from the registered configuration must be reported to the Deputy Chief Engineer (Infrastructure) within 24 hours.

2.2 Quay Walls and Apron
The total quay length is 2,850 linear metres. The quay wall structure is a combination of anchored sheet pile (Berths 01–07) and concrete caisson (Berths 08–12). The apron width varies between 25 and 40 metres. A routine visual inspection of the quay walls was carried out in the week of 15 June 2026. No structural defects requiring immediate intervention were noted. Minor spalling was observed at the expansion joint between Berth 05 and Berth 06; this has been logged for scheduled repair under Work Order WO-2026-0841.

2.3 Fendering Systems
The port utilises a mix of cone and cell fenders across all 12 berths. The fender inventory, including spare units, is maintained at the Engineering Stores. The following table summarises the fender types and their installation dates:

2.4 Bollards
A total of 96 bollards are installed across the 12 berths, with a nominal capacity of 100 tonnes each for the container and general cargo berths, and 150 tonnes for the bulk liquid berths. A load test verification of all bollards was last completed in November 2025. The test certificates are archived in the Engineering Document Control system. Bollard condition is checked during the weekly quay walkdown; the findings for June 2026 are recorded in the weekly inspection logs referenced in Section 5.0.

3.0 CRANE RAILS AND PAVEMENT

3.1 Crane Rails
The crane rail tracks for the ship-to-shore (STS) gantry cranes are laid on concrete beams. The rail alignment and gauge were surveyed in May 2026. The survey confirmed that the rail gauge is within the tolerance of ±5 mm across all berths. Rail wear measurements were taken at designated points; the maximum recorded wear is 8 mm on the landside rail at Berth 07. This is within the allowable wear limit of 12 mm. The next full rail survey is scheduled for November 2026.

3.2 Pavement
The container yard pavement (concrete interlocking blocks) is generally in good condition. Areas of settlement were previously identified at Yard B (near the reefer points). A patch repair was completed in March 2026. A follow-up inspection on 20 June 2026 confirmed that the repaired area is stable. No new significant settlement was observed in June. The asphalt pavement at the RoRo berth approach is scheduled for resurfacing in Q4 2026; the scope of work is being prepared by the Civil Engineering Unit.

**4.1 Berth Condition Summary**

The quay walls and berth structures were inspected during the monthly marine structures walkdown conducted on 22–23 June 2026. The inspection covered all 12 berths, with particular attention to the concrete copings, expansion joints, and the anchorages of the mooring hardware. The general condition of the concrete structures remains satisfactory, with no new structural defects identified beyond those previously logged. The findings of the June inspection are summarised in Table 4.1 below.

**4.2 Berth 5 Apapa – Maintenance Status**

Berth 5 Apapa maintenance_status scheduled maintenance. Record status: current. The scheduled maintenance for Berth 5 Apapa is currently active and has been planned to address the following scope of works:

- Replacement of the two neoprene bearing pads at the berth's western end, which have shown signs of compression set beyond the acceptable limit.
- Re-grouting of the anchor bolts for the bollards at positions B5-04 and B5-05.
- Application of a protective coating to the concrete coping along a 40-metre section where the existing coating has deteriorated.

The maintenance window is scheduled for 10–24 August 2026. During this period, Berth 5 Apapa will be unavailable for vessel berthing. The berthing schedule for this period has been adjusted by the Port Operations department to redistribute calls to Berths 4 and 6. The Engineering Department will issue a Notice to Mariners (NTM) and a port circular at least 14 days prior to the commencement of the works. The berth will be handed back to operations following a joint inspection by the Engineering Department and the Port Captain's office, which is planned for 25 August 2026.

**4.3 Mooring Hardware and Ancillary Equipment**

The inspection of mooring hardware, including bitts, quick-release hooks, and capstans, was completed on 24 June 2026. The findings are recorded below:

- **Quick-release hooks (QRH):** All 24 QRH units across the berths were functionally tested. Two units at Berth 09 were found to have a slower-than-specified release time and have been flagged for servicing. The servicing is scheduled for the next available maintenance window in July 2026.
- **Capstans:** The capstan motors at Berths 02, 07, and 11 were checked for current draw and temperature. All readings were within the normal operating range.
- **Bitts and bollards:** Visual inspection of the bitts and bollards found no signs of deformation or cracking. The bollard load test certificates remain valid as per the November 2025 verification.

documents.content:
The servicing has been rescheduled for the week commencing 19 October 2026, subject to parts receipt. Until the servicing is completed, the two QRH units at Berth 09 will remain in service but are subject to an operational restriction: they must be manually cycled once per shift to ensure the release mechanism does not seize. The Port Operations department has been notified of this restriction via internal memo dated 24 September 2026. The units will be re-tested for release time following the servicing.

2.3 Routine Inspections – September 2026

Routine visual inspections of all berth structures were carried out on 15 September 2026. No new structural defects were identified. The condition of fenders, mooring hooks, and bollard foundations remains consistent with the previous reporting period. The bollard load test certificates remain valid as per the November 2025 verification.

3.0 QUAY CRANE INVENTORY AND STATUS

The following table provides the current operational status of the quay cranes under the Engineering Department's remit as of 30 September 2026.

| Asset ID | Asset Name | Load Capacity (metric tons) | Maintenance Status | Next Scheduled Service |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------|------------------------|
| ENT16     | Quay Crane 7   | 50                          | Operational                          | 15 November 2026      |

3.1 Quay Crane 7 – Status and Inspection Record

Quay Crane 7 has a load_capacity_tons of 50 metric tons, according to the maintenance report. Record status: current. This rating is current and forms the basis for all operational load planning and lifting procedure approvals. No change to this rating is planned.

The crane was subject to its periodic three-monthly inspection on 10 September 2026. The inspection focused on the hoist braking system, the main trolley travel mechanism, and the condition of the wire ropes. The findings are as follows:

- **Hoist brakes:** The brake pads were measured at 70% of their original thickness, which is within the acceptable wear limit. The brake adjustment was verified and found to be within specification.
- **Trolley travel:** The travel wheels showed no abnormal wear. The rail alignment was checked and found to be within the tolerance of ±2 mm over the full length of travel.
- **Wire ropes:** The main hoist wire rope was inspected for broken wires and diameter reduction. No defects were found. The rope lubrication was topped up as part of the inspection.

A minor oil leak was observed on the slew gearbox oil seal. The leak is currently minor and does not affect the safe operation of the crane. The seal (Part No. SG-SE-118) has been ordered, and the replacement is scheduled for the next maintenance window in November 2026. The gearbox oil level is being monitored weekly until the seal is replaced.

The crane has been fully operational throughout the reporting period. No unplanned downtime was recorded.

4.0 PAVEMENT AND ROAD NETWORK

4.1 Container Yard Paving Repairs

The repair of the pavement in the container yard, specifically the area adjacent to the reefer stacks, was completed on 18 September 2026. The works involved the removal and replacement of a 25-square-metre section of concrete paving that had settled. The new concrete has been cured and is now open to traffic. The repaired area has been marked with temporary paint and will be monitored for any signs of settlement over the next three months.

LPC ENGINEERING MAINTENANCE REPORT – INFRASTRUCTURE OVERVIEW

**Report Period:** 1 June 2026 – 30 September 2026
**Date of Issue:** 2 October 2026
**Prepared by:** Engineering Department, Lagos Port Complex
**Distribution:** Port Manager, Head of Operations, Safety Officer, Chief Engineer

---

**5.0 DRAINAGE AND UTILITIES**

**5.1 Storm Water Drainage System**

Routine inspection of the main storm water drainage network was carried out on 14 August 2026. The inspection covered all open channels, culverts, and catch basins within the terminal operating area.

Findings:

- **Main outfall channel:** Clear of obstruction. Flow capacity assessed as adequate for current rainfall intensity.
- **Catch basins (Berths 1–4):** Two basins (CB-02 and CB-04) were found to be 40% silted. Desilting was carried out on 19 August 2026. Both basins are now clear.
- **Culvert under access road (Gate 2):** Minor cracking observed in the concrete headwall. Crack width measured at 2 mm. No active water ingress noted. The headwall is scheduled for patching during the November maintenance window.

No storm water pumping stations are currently out of service.

**5.2 Potable Water Supply**

The main potable water storage tank (Tank WT-01) was cleaned and disinfected on 27 July 2026. Water quality samples taken after cleaning were within WHO guidelines. The tank level control valve was serviced on the same date.

A leak was reported on the supply line serving the administration building on 3 September 2026. The leak was traced to a failed joint at the boundary wall. The joint was replaced on 5 September 2026. No further leaks have been reported.

**5.3 Sewerage System**

The sewage pumping station (SPS-01) serving the terminal buildings was inspected on 22 September 2026. Both pumps were found operational. Pump No. 2 was noted to have a higher than normal vibration level. Vibration analysis is scheduled for the next maintenance window. The station is operating normally.

**6.0 FENCING AND ACCESS CONTROL**

**6.1 Perimeter Fencing**

The perimeter fence along the eastern boundary was inspected on 11 August 2026. The inspection covered the full 1,200-metre length.

- **Concrete posts:** All posts in good condition.
- **Chain link mesh:** Two small breaches were found near the old customs checkpoint. These were repaired on 12 August 2026.
- **Barbed wire topping:** Intact throughout.

**6.2 Access Gates**

The four main access gates (Gates 1–4) were checked for mechanical operation on 17 September 2026. All gates open and close smoothly. Gate 3 hydraulic ram was found to be leaking a small amount of hydraulic fluid. The ram has been ordered (Part No. HR-G3-220) and will be replaced during the November maintenance window. The leak is minor and does not affect safe operation of the gate.

**7.0 BUILDING INFRASTRUCTURE**

**7.1 Administration Building**

Routine inspection of the administration building was carried out on 8 September 2026.

- **Roof:** No leaks reported. The roof drainage gutters were cleared of debris.
- **Air conditioning units:** All units serviced on 15 July 2026. Filters replaced. Units operating normally.
- **Electrical distribution board:** Thermal imaging scan carried out on 8 September 2026. No hot spots detected.

**7.2 Workshop Building**

The main workshop building roof was inspected on 21 August 2026 following a period of heavy rain. No leaks were found. The roller shutter doors were checked for operation. Door No. 2 was found to have a worn track. The track was replaced on 25 August 2026.
